title: Can a Vehicle Reach a Delivery Location
real_world_story: The dispatch system needs to know whether a vehicle can reach a particular delivery location through any sequence of roads. The road network is modeled as a directed graph. Use a depth-first traversal to determine whether the delivery location is reachable from the depot.

real_world_connection.start_represents: The depot from which the vehicle departs
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following roads as far as possible to discover whether a delivery is possible

problem_statement: Given a directed graph with N nodes and M edges, and two nodes D and T, determine whether there is a path from D to T. Print YES if T is reachable from D, otherwise print NO.
task: Use DFS to check whether the delivery location is reachable from the depot.
input_format: The first line contains four integers N, M, D and T, where N is the number of nodes (numbered 1 to N), M is the number of directed edges, D is the depot, and T is the delivery location. The next M lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a directed road from node U to node V.
output_format: Print YES if node T is reachable from node D, otherwise print NO.

examples.explanation: There is no road leading from node 1 toward node 4, so the delivery location is unreachable.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS explores one connected route as far as possible and can determine whether the target is reachable using recursion or an explicit stack.

hint: Begin the traversal at the depot node D.
Visit a neighbor and follow it as far as possible before backtracking.
If the delivery location T is visited, it is reachable.
real_world_takeaway: DFS helps a delivery company quickly confirm whether a vehicle can reach a delivery location, avoiding assignments for impossible routes.
